questions.question: Which of the following are examples of critically endangered wild plant species in India that are on the verge of extinction?
options: Madhuca insignis (a wild mahua) and Hubbardia heptaneuron (a grass species)
questions.explanation: Madhuca insignis is listed as Critically Endangered in World Flora Online's IUCN-sourced data. A 2015 field assessment by Botanical Survey of India researchers classified Hubbardia heptaneuron as Critically Endangered after confirming surviving populations at two Karnataka sites; the assessment described its very restricted range. The original pair is therefore retained, with the H. heptaneuron status explicitly attributed to the 2015 field assessment rather than presented as an undated universal status. This is supplementary botanical knowledge.

questions.subtopic: Genetic Diversity in Fisheries and Crops
questions.question: Why is the preservation of biodiversity crucial for the future of human agriculture and fisheries?
options: It ensures all crops grow without sunlight
It preserves the genetic diversity of wild relatives essential for breeding disease-resistant crops and robust aquatic species
It allows all marine fish to live in freshwater lakes
It prevents rivers from flowing into oceans
questions.explanation: NCERT explains that conservation protects genetic diversity in plants and animals, which supports the development and breeding of species. It also explicitly notes that fisheries depend heavily on maintaining aquatic biodiversity. The answer should not imply that biodiversity alone guarantees disease resistance or fishery productivity.
